newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Orange doubles mobile phone customers.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Orange doubles mobile phone customers.

text.p: British mobile telephone operator Orange Plc said on Monday that it had more than doubled its total subscribers to over 785,000 during 1996.
The company said it had added 125,000 customers to its all-digital network in the last three months of the year, its best ever quarter.
The figures confirm the positive trend in the British cellular market shown by both Vodafone Group and Cellnet, which is 60 percent owned by British Telecom.

Vodafone, the market leader in Britain, last week reported a 20 percent annual increase in subscriber numbers to some 2.8 million at end-December. Cellnet ended last year with 2.68 million customers, up from 2.3 million at the end of 1995.
Orange said it now had an 11.5 percent share of the total UK market, against seven percent at the end of 1995. Over 1996, it captured 29 percent of net market growth.
The company said its "churn" or disconnection rate of 18.6 percent in 1996 remained around a third lower than the industry average.
"We stay right on our plan for growth of subscribers, market share, usage, network coverage and churn," said managing director Hans Snook.
"We look forward in 1997 to continuing to move ahead and to extending our international service through new roaming agreements and the introduction of dual band handsets."
Finance Director Graham Howe told Reuters that the new handsets should be launched in the first half of 1997 and would extend potential coverage to most European countries.
Orange shares added 4p to 192p on Monday morning.
Orange, whose major shareholder remains Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa, was floated last March at a price of 205p.
